title: ScVal vector whose length prefix is 0xFFFFFFFF with no elements after it
caps_note: A cross-cutting encoding rule rather than a CAP: it applies to every XDR value of every protocol
why: The length prefix promises 4294967295 vector elements that the input does not contain. A decoder must compare the length with the remaining input before allocating; one that allocates first can be made to request a huge array by a few bytes of input.

source.reason: A vector length of 0xFFFFFFFF with no body; core checks the length against the input before allocating

notes: Probe vector 6h (evidence/sdk-matrix/vectors/vectors.json); it was run under the 1 GiB memory cap and under an address-space cap.

core_behaviour.evidence: stellar-core 30.0.0 print-xdr --filetype scval on the blob, run by hand for this entry: "Could not decode with type 'scval' : xvector overflow"
